title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
gist: Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5, a humanoid engineered to work safely near people without safety cages — it can move aside, freeze, or squat into a seated position when a human approaches — with early access in H1 2027 and general availability by end of 2027. The robot runs on Nvidia's Thor IGX compute plus the Nvidia Halos for Robotics safety stack, lifts 50 pounds, reaches 7.2 feet, and can work over 20 hours a day on a 90-minute battery that recharges in nine minutes.

insights.claim: Humanoid robots that can operate without isolated work cells and physical separation barriers unlock substantially more warehouse and automotive-factory deployment sites, because cage infrastructure is what limits where robots can be placed today.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Cage-free certification, not raw dexterity, is the variable that expands humanoid TAM — screen humanoid vendors on functional-safety progress first.
insights.quote: Such safety features could unlock many more opportunities to use such robots inside warehouses and automotive factories—all without requiring isolated robot work cells and physical separation barriers.
insights.locator: Agility Robotics has debuted its first humanoid robot

insights.claim: Agility cofounder Jonathan Hurst has called the safety issue a 'blocker for everybody' in humanoid robotics, framing the constraint as industry-wide rather than specific to any one vendor's hardware.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: If safety gates the whole category, whoever clears functional-safety certification first captures disproportionate early enterprise deployments regardless of demo quality.
insights.quote: the safety issue has been a “blocker for everybody,”
insights.locator: The competition to deploy humanoid robots has only intensified

insights.claim: Digit 5 implements graduated safety mitigations — moving to avoid a person, standing still, or squatting into a seated position depending on detected proximity — rather than the binary shut-down-and-restart approach used by earlier industrial robots.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Granular mitigation preserves uptime around humans, which is the difference between a robot that pencils out on throughput and one that does not.
insights.quote: The robot was designed with a complex safe motion system that can take a variety of different mitigations depending on exactly what sort of human presence is detected
insights.locator: When Agility’s new Digit 5 robot detects a person

insights.claim: Agility distinguishes 'cooperative safety' — robots and humans working productively in the same space at a safe distance — from the later-stage 'collaborative safety' where humanoids work directly in close proximity, defining a two-stage commercial roadmap.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Use the cooperative-to-collaborative ladder as the maturity yardstick when evaluating humanoid claims; most vendors are not yet at rung one.
insights.locator: Having a humanoid robot with such “cooperative safety” features

themes.theme: Nvidia dependency in the robot stack

insights.claim: Digit 5 runs on Nvidia's Thor IGX hardware for AI compute and integrates the Nvidia Halos for Robotics software stack for safety applications, with Agility describing itself as one of the first adopters taking Thor IGX through to a functionally safe application.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Nvidia is embedding itself in the functional-safety layer of humanoids, not just the compute layer — a stickier, certification-locked position than GPU sales alone.
insights.quote: Digit is equipped with this Thor IGX, and we’re one of the first adopters to be taking that through to a functionally safe application using that technology
insights.locator: Agility’s newest humanoid robot uses Nvidia’s Thor IGX

insights.claim: Agility CTO Pras Velagapudi declined to disclose the specific sensor types used to detect nearby humans, saying only that the array consists of 'a few different types of vision-based sensors,' indicating the perception stack is treated as competitive IP.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Vision-only (no disclosed lidar) human detection would be a notable cost-structure choice; sensor BOM is where humanoid unit economics are won or lost.
insights.quote: a few different types of vision-based sensors
insights.locator: Digit 5 uses AI algorithms along with an onboard set

insights.claim: Agility developed Digit 5's safety features while participating in the working group drafting ISO 25785-1, an international safety standard for industrial mobile robots now under committee review and headed for a vote by the organization's 89 voting nation members.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Co-authoring the standard you must comply with is a durable moat; track ISO 25785-1's vote as the regulatory catalyst for cage-free humanoid deployment.
insights.locator: Agility developed Digit 5’s safety features while also participating

insights.claim: Digit 5's upgraded legs let it repeatedly lift up to 50 pound loads, which covers all single-person lift tasks as defined by US Occupational Safety and Health Administration workplace safety regulations.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Pegging payload to the OSHA single-person lift threshold makes the labor-substitution pitch concrete and quantifies the addressable task set for buyers.
insights.locator: Beyond being designed to operate safely around humans

themes.theme: Duty cycle and deployment track record

insights.claim: Digit 5's battery lasts 90 minutes and recharges in nine minutes, enabling more than 20 hours of work within a 24-hour period — roughly a 10-to-1 work-to-charge ratio that approaches continuous operation.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A 20-hour daily duty cycle is the number that makes robot-versus-labor payback math work at three shifts; compare rival humanoids on this metric, not on peak runtime.
insights.quote: That enables Digit 5 to perform more than 20 hours of work within a 24-hour period by spending most of its time operating rather than charging.
insights.locator: The new humanoid robot also has a battery

insights.claim: Earlier Digit robots have accumulated more than 65,000 hours working at North American warehouses and factories since Agility became the first company to deploy humanoids in full-time commercial operations at a GXO warehouse in Atlanta in 2024.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: 65,000 field hours is a real reliability data set that differentiates Agility from demo-stage humanoid competitors when enterprises run procurement diligence.
insights.quote: earlier versions of the Digit robot have accumulated more than 65,000 hours working at warehouses and factories across North America
insights.locator: Since that time, earlier versions of the Digit robot

insights.claim: Agility's pilot and deployment client list includes GXO, Schaeffler, Amazon, and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, spanning third-party logistics, industrial components, e-commerce and automotive manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Cross-sector pilot logos suggest humanoid demand is not confined to one vertical, but pilots are not volume orders — watch for conversion in 2027.
insights.locator: Clients that have piloted or deployed the Digit robots

insights.claim: Digit 5 is scheduled for customer early access within the first half of 2027 and general availability by the end of that year, with Agility retooling its RoboFab facility in Salem, Oregon to produce it.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Meaningful humanoid revenue from this product is a 2027-2028 story; discount any 2026 humanoid revenue assumptions in the sector.
insights.quote: Customers can expect to gain early access to the Digit 5 within the first half of 2027, with the robot becoming generally available by the end of that year
insights.locator: Customers can expect to gain early access

insights.claim: Digit 5 stands 5 feet 11 inches and reaches up to 7.2 feet versus Digit 4's 5.5-foot reach, and adds swappable grippers so end-effectors can be quickly changed for different manipulation tasks.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Matching human shelf reach plus tool-changing means the robot fits existing warehouse racking without facility redesign — the hidden cost that kills most automation ROI.
insights.locator: Compared to the older Digit 4 robot
